Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexaWave Communications Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexaWave Communications's Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Network Officer; David Kim, Chief Commercial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3, demonstrating our continued commitment to growth and innovation. Our success is driven by our dedicated team and strategic investments. Our key achievements include delivering a robust EBITDA margin of 38.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year, alongside strong free cash flow generation tracking toward $8.7 billion for the year. We've made significant progress in 5G deployment, with $2.8 billion in capex driving 85% national coverage. Enterprise and B2B initiatives delivered $2.8 billion in revenue, up 18% year-over-year, with major wins like a $750 million private 5G contract. Effective operating expense management yielded $285 million in run-rate savings, boosting profitability. Our content and media segment hit $2.45 billion in revenue, with 48.2 million paid subscribers. Revenue mix shows diversification, with mobile at 42%, broadband 28%, media 15%, enterprise 10%, and emerging tech 5%. Finally, our dividend remains sustainable, covered 1.7x by FCF, with total shareholder returns at 7.8% TTM yield. The launch of our Unlimited Max 5G plan is exceeding expectations, resulting in 450,000 postpaid net adds and ARPU uplift. Further milestones are expanding our FTTH footprint to 55% of top MSAs and hitting 35 million streaming subs. We are also focusing on AI-powered network orchestration for opex leverage. Our dedication to vendor consolidation and AI chatbots is bearing fruit with $250 million in savings. Our strategy is to enhance 5G private networks for media clients. We are actively investing in edge CDN for low-latency streaming. We are also exploring sovereign cloud bundles and finally, analyzing regional margin variations to optimize returns.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. Now, let's review our financial performance. Revenue for the quarter reached $12.8 billion, reflecting a 6% increase year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $4.9 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.2%. We maintain a disciplined approach to cost management and capital allocation. Capital expenditures totaled $3.0 billion, primarily allocated to expanding our 5G network, fiber infrastructure, and content investments.

Good afternoon, everyone. As we turn to forward guidance, I'd like to provide some color on our EBITDA margin outlook, which remains a cornerstone of our profitability story in this dynamic telecom and media landscape. For context, we delivered that robust 38.2% consolidated EBITDA margin in Q3, up 210 basis points year-over-year, driven by strong wireless service revenue growth, opex efficiencies from our AI-powered network orchestration platform, and healthy advertising uplift in our streaming segment amid peak sports programming.

Looking ahead to Q4 2024, we are guiding to an EBITDA margin of 39.5% to 40.5%. This represents sequential expansion of 130 to 230 basis points, putting us on track for our strongest quarterly margin in company history. On the top line, we expect total revenue growth of 4% to 5% quarter-over-quarter, anchored by postpaid phone net adds of 450,000 to 550,000—fueled by our Unlimited Max 5G plan, which now penetrates 45% of our base and is lapping promotional pricing from last year. Media revenue should contribute another leg, with our streaming subs hitting 35 million paid, up 15% YoY, thanks to exclusive NFL Sunday Ticket synergies similar to what we've seen at Paramount Global.

Margin tailwinds here are multifaceted. First, opex leverage: We've realized $250 million in run-rate savings YTD from our 'NetworkNext' initiative, which deploys machine learning algorithms—much like Verizon's Intelligent Edge Network—to dynamically allocate spectrum across our C-band and mmWave assets, reducing energy costs by 18% in high-traffic urban cells. This is scaling nationally, with ROI already exceeding 3x. Second, fixed cost absorption from fiber overbuilds: Our FTTH footprint now covers 55% of our top 50 MSAs, akin to AT&T's 40+ million locations passed, driving fixed broadband ARPU to $85, up from $78 a year ago, with churn below 1%. Regionally, U.S. markets like the Northeast are leading at 42% sub-margins, while our Latin American ops—think Mexico and Brazil, where we've mirrored Claro's playbook—are at 35%, benefiting from currency tailwinds and 4G LTE densification.

Offsetting some pressure, we'll see modest seasonal marketing spend for holiday bundles, and handset costs remain elevated due to supply chain normalization post-Qualcomm Snapdragon shortages. Capex intensity stays at 18% of revenue, focused on 5G Ultra Wideband midband rollout to 85% coverage.

For the full FY 2025, our EBITDA margin guidance is 40% to 42%, implying 170 to 380 basis points of expansion from 2024's expected 38.5%. This is predicated on consolidated revenue growth of 5% to 7%, with wireless core at mid-single digits, broadband accelerating to 8-10% via hybrid coax-to-fiber upgrades, and media delivering 12-15% from ad-loaded tiers and content licensing—leveraging our Warner Bros. Discovery-style studio partnerships for originals like 'Edge of Tomorrow' sequels.

Strategically, this guidance embeds several key initiatives. Enterprise edge: We're targeting 20% growth in 5G private networks for media production, partnering with the likes of AWS Outposts for low-latency cloud integration, which boosts service margins to 55%. Cost transformation: Phase 2 of our vendor consolidation—already cut 15% from tower leases à la Crown Castle renegotiations—will deliver another $400 million in savings, with AI chatbots handling 70% of customer care, dropping CAC by 22%. On the media side, combating Netflix-level churn through personalized recommendation engines powered by our 5G dataset will stabilize at sub-4%.

Regionally, North America drives 65% of EBITDA at 43% margins, buoyed by spectrum premiumization post-Auctions 108/110. Europe (via our Vodafone JV echoes) guides to 37%, navigating Ofcom price caps but gaining from 5G SA standalone launches. APAC and emerging markets at 32% reflect higher competitive intensity from Reliance Jio but offset by eSIM roaming revenue up 25%.

Headwinds to monitor include regulatory scrutiny on net neutrality redux, potential FCC universal service fees inflation, and cord-cutting pressures—though our bundled 'NexaStream + 5G Home' packages have stabilized video ARPU at $18. We see no material forex drag, assuming USD strength moderates.

Today, I'd also like to dive deep into our free cash flow generation and utilization, which remains a cornerstone of our financial strength and our ability to deliver consistent shareholder value in this dynamic telecom and media landscape. For the full year 2024 guidance, we're on track to generate approximately $8.7 billion in free cash flow on a levered basis, up 21% from $7.2 billion in 2023. This marks our sixth consecutive year of FCF growth, underscoring the resilience of our hybrid telecom-media model amid 5G monetization ramps, streaming subscriber tailwinds, and disciplined cost management.

In Q3 alone, we delivered $2.4 billion in FCF, a 15% quarter-over-quarter increase and well ahead of our $2.1 billion guide. Trailing twelve months FCF now stands at $8.5 billion. The primary drivers are multifaceted: Operational efficiency and revenue mix shift, with adjusted EBITDA growing 8% year-over-year to $4.9 billion in Q3, fueled by a 4% rise in wireless ARPU to $58.20, driven by our Unlimited Max 5G plans—now adopted by 65% of our postpaid base, similar to Verizon's myPlan momentum. Broadband ARPU held steady at $72 in our U.S. fiber markets, bolstered by 15% y/y subscriber growth in FTTH deployments. On the media side, NexaStream added 1.2 million net adds in Q3, reaching 28 million subs, with ARPU up 7% to $14.50 from premium tier upselling and ad-supported tiers à la Netflix's strategy. This diversified our revenue streams, with wireless at 52%, broadband 28%, and media/content 20%—reducing cyclicality.

Working capital optimization improved days sales outstanding by 5 days to 42, thanks to streamlined billing on our OSS/BSS upgrades with Amdocs platforms. Inventory turns improved 12% in our device supply chain, mitigating lingering chip shortages. CapEx discipline saw total CapEx for Q3 at $3.0 billion, or 18% of revenue, down from 20% last year as we lap peak 5G radio investments. We allocated 55% to wireless, focusing on C-band spectrum utilization in the U.S. now at 85% coverage, on par with AT&T; 30% to broadband for new FTTH homes passed; and 15% to media for edge CDN builds with Akamai.

Regionally, North America contributed 72% of FCF, with U.S. wireless postpaid churn at 0.76%—better than Comcast's Xfinity Mobile. Europe added strong growth on 5G Standalone core launches, and APAC yielded incremental cash from towerco monetization.

Turning to utilization, of our YTD FCF, we've deployed 62% to shareholder returns with $2.1 billion in dividends at 4.2% yield, covered 2.8x by FCF, plus $2.1 billion in buybacks under our $10 billion authorization; 22% to debt reduction, lowering net debt/EBITDA to 2.3x; 12% to growth reinvestments like Open RAN pilots and content slates; and the rest to taxes.

This balanced approach has returned significant value while funding 5G leadership. We're guiding $8.5-9.0 billion full-year FCF.

Let me also provide a detailed breakdown of our revenue mix by segment, highlighting the percentage contributions, year-over-year trends, and strategic drivers. For Q3 2024, total revenue reached $12.8 billion, up 6% YoY. Our mix is diversified: Mobile Services at 42%, Broadband & Wireline at 28%, Media & Entertainment at 15%, Enterprise & Wholesale at 10%, and Emerging Technologies at 5%. This shift reflects our pivot toward higher-margin digital services.

Mobile Services: 42% ($5.4B, +4.8% YoY), driven by postpaid net adds and ARPU to $52.30. North America 78%, Europe 15%, APAC growing 12%.

Broadband & Wireline: 28% ($3.6B, +12.4% YoY), with fiber net adds and RBA to $78. North America 65%, Europe 20%.

Media & Entertainment: 15% ($1.9B, +18.7% YoY), DTC subs to 28 million, ARPU $14.50. North America 70%.

Enterprise & Wholesale: 10% ($1.3B, -2.1% YoY), offset by 5G private networks.

Emerging Technologies: 5% ($640M, +52% YoY), IoT and FWA.

This evolution supports margin expansion and $8-10 billion FCF.

Turning to dividend sustainability and shareholder returns, a cornerstone of our strategy. We declared a quarterly dividend of $0.65 per share, or $2.60 annualized, yielding 4.5%—among the highest in peers. Payout ratio at 58% of EPS, FCF coverage 1.7x on $11.2 billion TTM FCF. FY2024 FCF $12.0-$12.5 billion implies stronger coverage.

Leverage at 2.4x net debt/EBITDA, capex 15% of revenue. Regionally solid across NA, Europe, APAC. YTD $2.1 billion buybacks, total yield 7.8%, TSR beating peers. Framework: 60% incremental FCF to returns, 30% debt, 10% M&A. Rock-solid through cycles.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you. I'm pleased to provide an update on our network advancements. We've significantly expanded our 5G coverage, delivering faster speeds and lower latency. Our network reliability remains high, and we are continuously optimizing our infrastructure to meet growing demand. We are also focusing on enhancing our cybersecurity posture. We are committed to aggressively advancing our 5G Standalone architecture to unlock ultra-low latency for immersive media, AR/VR, and cloud gaming.

For Q3 2024, we deployed $2.8 billion in CapEx, 28% of revenue, up 12% YoY, with 45% or $1.26 billion to 5G: $850 million RAN, $300 million core, $110 million backhaul. YTD $8.4 billion toward $11-11.5 billion full-year.

Progress: 85% national 5G coverage across 320 million POPs, sub-6 C-band and mmWave. Northeast/Midwest 98% SA with 1.2 Gbps speeds for 8K streaming; Sunbelt/West 92% with FWA trials; rural 65% via DSS to 75% year-end.

Virtualized 70% core with Ericsson, latency <5ms; slicing live in 15 markets; O-RAN 10% sites. Multi-vendor: 45% Ericsson, 35% Nokia. Spectral efficiency +25% YoY, data traffic +35%.

5G subs +42% to 45 million, $1.2 billion ARPU incremental. ROI 18-22%. Q4 CapEx $2.6 billion, 2025 $10.5-11 billion toward SDN/private 5G.

David Kim: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We've seen strong subscriber growth across our various service offerings. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, and we are continuously improving the customer experience. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships to offer bundled services and enhance customer value. We are prioritizing our Enterprise and B2B segment, a bright spot delivering $2.8 billion in Q3 revenue, up 18% YoY and 5% QoQ. ARPU to $45,000 annually, +12%; 1,200 net new customers to 28,000, churn <2%.

Key wins: $750 million 5-year private 5G with GlobalBank for edge AI; $450 million MediaEdge CDN with StreamCo boosting throughput 25%; $320 million IoT/V2X with AutoTech.

NA 65% revenue +22%; EMEA +25%; APAC +14%; LatAm +30% QoQ. Initiatives: 5G suite unlocking $400 million ARR; SecureEdge cybersecurity; media transformation +35% growth. Pipeline $15 billion, FY25 growth 20+% at 65% margins.

Lisa Chen: Thank you. From a technology perspective, we are focused on driving innovation and leveraging emerging technologies to transform our business. We are exploring the use of AI and machine learning to automate network operations, improve customer service, and develop new products and services. We are also investing in research and development to stay ahead of the curve. Our technological direction is toward AI personalization in streaming and 5G-optimized content delivery.

Raj Patel: Thank you. Operationally, we are focused on improving efficiency and streamlining our processes. We are leveraging data analytics to optimize our resource allocation and improve decision-making. We are also committed to sustainability and reducing our environmental impact. Our operational focus is on operating expense management initiatives delivering $285 million run-rate savings in Q3, down 7% YoY OpEx to fuel 180 bps EBITDA margin expansion to 38.2%.

Network optimization (45% savings): SDN/NFV across 65% U.S. wireless, -22% hardware, $45 million YoY save; FTTH Open RAN -18% backhaul. NA $77 million, APAC $25 million.

Vendor consolidation (25%): 12-15% concessions, $71 million save, LATAM $32 million.

Customer service automation (20%): GenAI handles 45% inquiries, -15% agents, $35 million; media ad ops -20%.

Workforce/real estate (10%): Hybrid model $18 million save, retraining +11% productivity.

Net impact: EBITDA +$260 million YoY, FCF $2.4 billion, ROIC +220 bps to 11.2%. H2 $350 million more savings toward 40%+ margins.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more details on your content strategy and your plans for investing in original programming, and what is the anticipated impact on subscriber growth?

Alex Rivera: Good morning, John. Our content and media segment is a high-growth engine, with Q3 revenue at $2.45 billion, up 18% YoY and 5% QoQ from SVOD StreamHub, AVOD, linear sports, and licensing. Subs hit 48.2 million paid, +2.8 million net adds, churn 4.2%. Subscription $1.62 billion +22%, ARPU $13.75; ads $620 million +12%; licensing $230 million. Blended ARPU $12.42, SAC $45.

NA $2.08 billion +20%, 1.9 million adds from NFL rights; EMEA/ LATAM/APAC strong localized growth. EBITDA $825 million, 33.7% margin +400 bps from scale, content amortization down to 28%.

Strategy: AI recommendations +15% session time; 5G NBA broadcasts; bundling uplift $8 ARPU; PixelForge acquisition, Charter deals. Q4 guide $2.55-2.65 billion, 34-36% margins. Originals like our slate drive 17-21% growth, targeting 2-3 million quarterly adds.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your plans for addressing the digital divide and ensuring that all communities have access to affordable broadband, and how do you plan to achieve rural coverage targets?

David Kim: Hi Emily. We're tackling the digital divide head-on through FWA and FTTH expansions, with rural coverage at 65% now via DSS, targeting 75% year-end with Nokia AirScale. FWA trials serve 150,000 households at 500 Mbps, competing in underserved areas. Bundled NexaStream + 5G Home stabilizes ARPU, while partnerships ensure affordability. This supports enterprise media caching and aligns with our 40% broadband penetration goal by 2025.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson: Can you discuss your capital allocation priorities and your plans for returning capital to shareholders, including buyback plans?

Jordan Lee: Thanks, Mike. Our FCF-first framework prioritizes 60% to returns: $2.1 billion YTD dividends covered 2.8x, $2.1 billion buybacks under $10 billion program, retiring shares for $0.85 EPS accretion. Debt reduction to 2.3x leverage, growth like Open RAN, then taxes. FY2024 FCF $8.5-9.0 billion supports $0.85 quarterly dividends and $5-7 billion buybacks annually, opportunistic ahead of M&A.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Park with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Park: What are your strategies for navigating the changing regulatory landscape?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Lisa. We're proactively engaging on net neutrality, FCC fees, EU DMA, and price caps. Our diversified model, spectrum holdings, and compliance investments like GDPR-ready SecureEdge position us well. Partnerships and O-RAN reduce vendor risks, while FCF buffers auction costs. We're gaining share through innovation amid scrutiny.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In conclusion, we are pleased with our performance this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We are committed to innovation, customer satisfaction, and sustainability. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
